To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human adipose stromatal cells (hADCS) are more potent than human bone marrow stromatal cells (HBMC) in mediating neovascularization in response to vascular ischemia.
human adipose stromatal cells (hADCS) are better than human bone marrow stromatal cells (BMSC) for mediating neovascularization in response to hindlimb ischemias in a nude mice.

human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hADMSCs) have better angiogenic activity than human bone-marrow-derived mesenchymalmal stem cells (HBMSCs) and that the angiogenic activity of hADMSCs is due, at least in part, to higher expression and secretion of matrix metalloproteinases 3 and 9.

the development of new strategies for the prevention of ischemia-induced tissue damage.
the comparison of angiogenic potency between hADSCs and hBMSCs in a hindlimb ischemic model.
the development of a new method for the treatment of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hADSC is a better candidate than hBMSC for therapeutic angiogenesis, and that the proangiogenic effect of hADSC is mediated through MMPs.
hADSC are more potent in mediating neovascularization than hBMSC in response to hindlimb ischemic condition.

adipose stromal cell (hADSC)-derived conditioned media (hADSCCM) has superior in vitro and in vivo angiogenic potency to bone marrow stromal cell-derived conditioned media (hBMSCCM) in a nude mice ischemia model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hADSC are more effective than hBMSC in mediating angiogenesis in hindlimb ishemia.

hADSC transplantation is more effective than hBMSC transplantation in the recovery of blood flow and tissue injury in the hindlimb ischemic nude mice, and this difference may be due to the difference of MMP expression between hADSCs and hBMSCs.
hADSC transplantation is more potent than hBMSC in mediating neovascularization in response to ischemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hADSC are more potent than hBMSC in promoting neovascularization and that this difference is due to higher expression of MMPs in hADSC than hBMSC, which are important mediators of neovascularization.
hADSC is superior to hBMSC in mediating neovascularization in response to hindlimb ischemic injury.
